display_long_description:
Graffiti Phoenix takes your spray cans to the walls valley writers know.

FOUR PHOENIX PLACES
- ROOSEVELT ROW: a mural alley in the downtown arts district on a gold afternoon. Paint bungalow galleries and a brick corner block under colourful shade sails and string lights, with a container gallery at the end.
- ARIZONA CANAL: down in the dry canal bed during the winter drain-down. Five-metre concrete walls, a road bridge overhead, palms along the banks, Camelback glowing pink at blue hour and bats pouring out of the storm drain.
- MONSOON: an abandoned desert drive-in at sunset. The giant screen, the old snack bar, rows of speaker posts and rusted cars, a tumbleweed rolling through, and a monsoon storm with lightning and rolling thunder.
- TEMPE MILL: the old flour mill on the lake on a crystal morning. Painted silos rise beside you, freights cross the trestle overhead and hot-air balloons drift over the water.

THE CITY IS ALIVE
People walk the alley, watch the bats, photograph the storm and stop to look at your work.

PAINT IT
Eight CITIVIEW spray cans, skinny, medium and fat caps, 32 stencils including A to Z, real mist and drips on 20 walls of brick, stucco, block, concrete and steel. Take a photo of your piece and switch places from the menu.
